summary: The p6 task-vector sign inference is invalid; numerical narratives overstate uniform preservation and the stopping rule conflicts. These are local demonstrated problems. The empirical six-task robustness advantage is not refuted. Scalar guarantees, historical implementation, units and broader/adaptive robustness need evidence.
limitations: No author code or model execution and no empirical reproduction.
Separate OpenReview supplementary attachment inaccessible (403); existence unresolved.
Pinned release lacks an identified ILU/RMU training implementation, downstream convergence/RA code and historical result/timing bindings.
No weights/datasets acquired; five preparation-excluded data payloads remain excluded.

problems.title: Cosine-sign criteria do not imply opposing directions
problems.assumptions: Nonzero u,f,d; only cos(u,f)<0 is assumed. d=theta_uft-theta_u is an increment.
problems.check: Independent exact 2D u=(1,0),f=(-1/2,sqrt3/2),d=u+f. All norms1; cos(u,f)=-.5,cos(d,u)=cos(d,f)=.5. Final projection u.(u+d)=||u||²+||u||||d||cos(d,u).
problems.result: Both sign diagnostics hold; positive alignment with f need not imply negative alignment with u. Reported ILU own cosines .09,.3554 show same signs. Gram triples feasible.
problems.counterevidence: No universal theorem supplied; the task-vector analysis is descriptive explanation. Reported empirical FQ gains do not rely on the false geometric inference.
problems.impact: Local mechanistic diagnostic needs correction; no demonstrated core guarantee or optimizer dependency, so Minor, not a claim all empirical conclusions fail.
problems.correction: Exact corrected projection identity proved; functional forgetting still needs loss/norm/trajectory evidence. No replacement robustness theorem.
problems.repair_verification: Exact corrected projection identity proved; functional forgetting still needs loss/norm/trajectory evidence. No replacement robustness theorem.
